topic: Matched honest nuclear-radius frontier for staggered low-rank panels under iid noise: under fixed deterministic adoption, known fixed rank, iid Gaussian cell errors, normalized strong-factor/incoherence bounds, and quantitative overlap Grams, define the minimax expected observable nuclear-error radius over all uniformly honest procedures. Characterize it up to constants with a polynomial-time wedge-aware spectral certificate and a same-class all-procedure lower bound; keep the exact rate answer-open. Derive only a coverage-valid diffuse-weight ATT corollary by nuclear/operator duality. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: the exact block identity Gamma_IQ=Gamma_IP Gamma_CP^dagger Gamma_CQ and balanced rank-one analysis suggest scale sigma sqrt(n), far below diameter n. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: matching tangent packing for every admissible wedge. EARLY KILL TEST: matching sigma_+ sqrt(n) bounds for the balanced rank-one L-mask.

open_problems.open_problem: In the balanced rank-one L-shaped mask with fixed positive row and column overlap fractions, is the minimax expected uniformly honest nuclear-error radius of order sigma times the square root of the panel side length rather than the order-n parameter-space diameter?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing block-completion results control Frobenius RMSE, individual cells, or treatment-effect averages rather than the radius of a uniformly honest nuclear ball. Summing entrywise intervals gives an order-n bound and discards the fact that rank-one missing-cell errors share estimated row and column directions. Proving the conjectured sigma-square-root-n scale requires a joint singular-value analysis of this correlated low-rank error and uniform control of nonlinear factor-rotation remainders; the matching lower bound must cover all procedures rather than only a chosen completion estimator.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Finite-sample constants c and C such that the balanced rank-one L-mask minimax expected honest nuclear radius lies between c sigma sqrt(n) and C sigma sqrt(n), together with a computable attaining radius.

writing_exemplar.why: Its block-missing phase-transition framing is the closest narrative for isolating a decisive balanced benchmark before treating a full staircase.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Structured missing blocks arise in causal panels -> completion exhibits sharp phase behavior -> existing error analysis is Frobenius or coordinatewise -> determine the honest nuclear-radius scale in the simplest L-mask.

method_exemplars.technique: Use four-block SVD transport, derive a non-asymptotic Gaussian linearization, and retain the joint covariance of the shared factor errors.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It analyzes the same L-mask and iid-noise geometry sharply; the new step is replacing a scalar projection with the nuclear norm of the collective low-rank error.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate factors from a tall block, loadings from a wide block, align their rotations through the overlap, and expand imputation error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At rank one, its expansion exposes the shared row and column error components that could produce the proposed sub-diameter nuclear scale.

method_exemplars.technique: Reduce honest nuclear-radius lower bounds to testing and construct low-rank alternatives with controlled Gaussian divergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the all-procedure confidence-set lower-bound logic needed to validate the balanced benchmark.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the minimax expected data-dependent radius of a uniformly honest nuclear-norm confidence ball for a known-rank low-rank panel observed through a fixed staggered-adoption wedge with iid Gaussian cell noise?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest causal-panel inference is entrywise or functional-specific, while available confidence-set theory uses random-entry or isotropic Gaussian trace-regression designs. A deterministic staircase observation operator is anisotropic: its near-null tangent directions vary with adoption timing and overlap Grams, while nuclear loss aggregates correlated errors across the entire missing wedge. Known rank removes rank-adaptation as the principal obstruction but does not determine this wedge-specific modulus of continuity. The scan found no result combining fixed staggered masks, uniform honesty, nuclear loss, a polynomial-time certificate, and a matching all-procedure lower bound.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A two-sided theorem characterizing the minimax expected honest nuclear radius up to universal constants as an explicit function of noise, dimensions, rank, and overlap-Gram parameters, with a polynomial-time attaining procedure and a same-class lower bound over all procedures.

writing_exemplar.why: Its narrative moves from staggered counterfactual missingness to computational inference and instance-optimality, closely matching the desired transition from entrywise width to a global radius.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Staggered adoption hides untreated potential outcomes -> low rank couples observed and missing cells -> practical inference needs computable uncertainty -> characterize the smallest honest global nuclear-error radius.

method_exemplars.technique: Combine four-block SVD transport, Gaussian approximation of the linearized error, and a Bayesian Cramer-Rao instance-wise lower bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It solves the same deterministic staggered missing-data problem at the entrywise level, making its block decomposition the nearest machinery to lift to nuclear loss.

method_exemplars.technique: Convert honest-confidence diameter into a composite testing problem and construct nuclear-separated alternatives at controlled Gaussian divergence.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired converse is also a confidence-radius lower bound in nuclear norm, with the fixed wedge replacing isotropic measurements.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias low-rank completion estimates and prove sharp distributional approximations through convex-nonconvex coupling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides an efficient noisy matrix uncertainty-quantification template whose random-sampling geometry must be replaced by wedge-aware spectral control.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct, for every quantitatively admissible staggered wedge, a fixed-rank incoherent tangent packing whose observed-cell Gaussian divergences remain bounded while its nuclear separations match the wedge-aware upper radius?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior CausalSmith converses show that an all-procedure bound must use a restriction-preserving hard submodel and control divergence in the actual observable experiment. Existing Schatten-loss packings instead exploit isotropic measurements, while staggered-panel lower bounds localize individual entries. For a staircase mask, each alternative must remain on the known-rank manifold, preserve strong-factor, incoherence, and overlap-Gram constraints, remain nearly invisible on observed cells, and accumulate nuclear separation over the missing wedge. The first failing step is the choice of a universal tangent basis: admissible near-null directions rotate with each wedge's overlap Grams, so the balanced rank-one construction does not establish a uniform converse.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform Le Cam, Fano, Assouad, or Bayesian-prior lemma indexed by overlap Grams that preserves the full model class, bounds observed Gaussian divergence, and produces nuclear separation matching the proposed spectral upper radius up to constants.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames confidence-radius impossibility through the corresponding testing boundary, making the tangent-packing obstacle visibly load-bearing.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Honest confidence sets imply tests -> tests require separated alternatives with small divergence -> nuclear geometry determines the separation boundary -> fixed wedges require a new restriction-preserving tangent packing.

method_exemplars.technique: Use Ingster-type mixture alternatives and reduce honest confidence diameter to testing risk.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It directly converts nuclear-separated low-rank alternatives into a lower bound for honest radii.

method_exemplars.technique: Parameterize locally around the true factors and apply a Bayesian Cramer-Rao bound to the observed four-block experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its tangent calculation respects staggered observation geometry but must be enlarged from one coordinate to collective nuclear separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct minimax packings on intersections of rank and boundedness classes under noisy trace regression.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the global low-rank minimax template whose isometry argument must be replaced by wedge-specific Gram control.

open_problems.open_problem: Can four-block SVD transport be assembled across an arbitrary staggered staircase into a polynomial-time, fully observable nuclear-error certificate without paying a triangle-inequality factor in the number of adoption cohorts?

open_problems.why_unsolved: Cohortwise assembly of entrywise or blockwise bounds adds nuclear norms and can grow with the number of adoption cohorts even though adjacent errors share estimated singular subspaces and overlap data. The four-block argument analyzes scalar projections, so the first changed step is a joint singular-value bound for correlated staircase error with all tuning quantities observable. A prior CausalSmith construction obtains an exact certificate from compact primal-dual decision sets and complementary support; transferring that idea requires replacing its finite endpoint-orbit reduction with a continuous low-rank program whose dual remains computable without knowing the singular vectors. No located result supplies such a cohort-count-free observable certificate.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A polynomial-time spectral or semidefinite procedure returning an estimator, an observable dual certificate, and a radius with uniform nuclear-error coverage and no avoidable multiplicative dependence on the number of cohorts.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents four-block SVD transport as a practical computational building block for inference under staggered adoption.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: A staircase decomposes into overlapping four-block problems -> SVD transport makes each local problem tractable -> local intervals do not certify collective matrix error -> exploit shared subspaces to obtain a global observable nuclear certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Use SVD-based four-block transport with explicit Gaussian leading terms and observable variance calibration.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the source construction to assemble; the changed proof step replaces one-coordinate approximation by a joint operator/nuclear perturbation bound.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias low-rank completion estimates and couple convex solutions to nonconvex factor estimates for sharp distributional control.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The convex-nonconvex bridge could preserve computation while exposing the shared global low-rank error.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply clip-constrained nuclear-norm minimization under deterministic masks and analyze mask-specific stability.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It demonstrates polynomial-time deterministic-mask recovery, but its qualitative asymptotics must be strengthened to finite-noise wedge-specific coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Are the smallest eigenvalues of cohort-by-time overlap Gram matrices, together with rank and panel dimensions, sufficient and essentially necessary to characterize nuclear-radius inflation for every deterministic staggered wedge?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The literature uses non-equivalent descriptions of overlap: tall-wide strong-factor conditions, observed-submatrix singular values, observation proportions, and graphon density. No located result proves that a finite list of overlap Gram spectra completely controls global nuclear uncertainty. Local Gram invertibility may coexist with coherent propagation of errors across several blocks, while a small eigenvalue need not generate a legal incoherent fixed-rank perturbation attaining the predicted blow-up. Thus both sufficiency for an upper certificate and necessity through a matching tangent direction remain unsettled.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessity-and-sufficiency theorem, or an explicit counterexample, determining whether admissible wedges with comparable overlap-Gram spectra have comparable minimax honest nuclear radii and quantifying divergence as a Gram eigenvalue approaches zero.

writing_exemplar.why: It organizes deterministic completion around an intrinsic observation-pattern condition and explicitly motivates a finite-sample quantitative successor.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Random-mask assumptions miss structured panels -> deterministic recovery needs an intrinsic mask invariant -> graphon density resolves asymptotic recoverability -> staggered panels need a finite-sample Gram invariant for honest nuclear uncertainty.

method_exemplars.technique: Split staggered missing cells into estimable groups, regularize and debias, and express functional variance through observed-factor Gram inverses.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its formulas show directly how overlap-Gram conditioning enters staggered causal-panel inference.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate tall-wide factors and align rotations through an observed overlap block before deriving a componentwise error expansion.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The proposed Gram frontier is a quantitative version of the overlap condition making this block transport possible.

method_exemplars.technique: Use algebraically verifiable combinatorial conditions for finite and unique rank-r completion under deterministic sampling.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a necessity-oriented deterministic-mask template against which a spectral Gram characterization can be tested.

open_problems.open_problem: For diffuse deterministic ATT weight matrices supported on the treated wedge, when does nuclear/operator duality yield a uniformly honest confidence interval whose length is rate-comparable to direct functional estimators under the same low-rank staggered-panel class?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The deterministic inequality relating a weighted error to the operator norm of its weight matrix transfers coverage immediately from a nuclear ball, but it does not establish statistical sharpness. Direct functional methods exploit the influence direction of the chosen ATT weights and may yield much shorter intervals, while one global ball protects many contrasts simultaneously. The unresolved obstacle is to identify a precise diffuseness and wedge-alignment regime in which the dual interval is rate-comparable, or to exhibit an unavoidable separation, including treated-outcome noise in the comparison.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A uniform coverage theorem with interval length bounded explicitly by the operator norm of the ATT weights times the nuclear radius, accompanied by a matching or separating minimax lower bound relative to direct ATT inference over a stated diffuse-weight class.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference through concrete staggered-adoption causal functionals and distinguishes individual effects from general bilinear targets.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Policy adoption is staggered -> untreated counterfactuals are low-rank missing entries -> empirical targets are weighted treatment-effect summaries -> determine when a global nuclear certificate gives honest competitive ATT intervals.

method_exemplars.technique: Debias a convex low-rank estimator in the treatment-mask direction, prove asymptotic normality, and establish rate optimality under alignment conditions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the natural direct-functional benchmark against which the operator-dual interval should be compared.

method_exemplars.technique: Propagate four-block low-rank estimation error into prescribed-coverage intervals for bilinear treatment-effect functionals.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It targets the same staggered weighted effects and supplies the closest functional-specific variance benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Use non-asymptotic concentration and robust conic optimization to cover staggered synthetic-control predictands uniformly over post-treatment periods.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its uniform-coverage construction is an alternative finite-sample benchmark for the value of a nuclear-ball-derived ATT interval.

literature_map:
Athey et al. (2021, JASA, arXiv:1710.10251) establish nuclear-norm matrix completion as a causal-panel estimator accommodating staggered missingness, but emphasize estimation rather than honest global uncertainty.
Bai and Ng (2021, JASA, arXiv:1910.06677) obtain tall-wide factor imputation and asymptotic laws under strong factors in the relevant observed subblocks.
Xiong and Pelger (2023, Journal of Econometrics, arXiv:1910.08273) give PCA-based inference under general adoption patterns; Su and Wang (2025, Journal of Econometrics, DOI:10.1016/j.jeconom.2025.106022) give unified least-squares asymptotics for block and staggered missingness.
Choi and Yuan (2024, JASA, arXiv:2308.02364) handle MNAR staggered panels by grouped nuclear regularization and debiasing, with variance controlled by observed-factor Gram inverses.
Yan and Wainwright (2024, arXiv:2401.13665) are the closest sharp result: four-block SVD inference is non-asymptotic and instance-optimal for individual missing entries via a Bayesian Cramer-Rao lower bound.
Xia, Yan, and Wainwright (2024, arXiv:2412.09482) extend that machinery to individual effects and bilinear causal functionals but do not form a global nuclear confidence ball.
Farias, Li, and Peng (2021, NeurIPS, arXiv:2106.02780) directly estimate average effects for general intervention masks and prove rate optimality and asymptotic normality.
Ben-Michael, Feller, and Rothstein (2022, JRSSB, arXiv:1912.03290) show staggered ATT error depends on unit-specific and pooled imbalance, motivating diffuse-weight functionals.
Cattaneo, Feng, Palomba, and Titiunik (2025, Review of Economics and Statistics, arXiv:2210.05026) provide non-asymptotic uniform post-treatment synthetic-control intervals through robust optimization.
Chatterjee (2020, IEEE TIT, arXiv:1910.01079) gives a necessary-and-sufficient asymptotic theory for deterministic masks and explicitly leaves the proper non-asymptotic formulation open.
Pimentel-Alarcon, Boston, and Nowak (2016, JSTSP, arXiv:1503.02596) give algebraic and combinatorial deterministic-mask conditions for finite and unique completion.
Koltchinskii, Tsybakov, and Lounici (2011, Annals of Statistics, arXiv:1011.6256) obtain near-minimax noisy completion rates under isometry in expectation; Chen, Fan, Ma, and Yan (2019, PNAS, arXiv:1906.04159) add debiased inference under random sampling.
Carpentier et al. (2018, Bernoulli, arXiv:1608.04861) construct honest adaptive Frobenius confidence sets for random completion designs; Carpentier and Nickl (2015, EJS, arXiv:1507.03829) show nuclear-norm rank adaptation can be impossible.
Capponi and Stojnic (2024, arXiv:2401.00578) derive asymptotic worst-case Frobenius RMSE and phase transitions for one missing block, not finite-sample honest nuclear radii under deterministic factor geometry.
The live intersection remains fixed deterministic staircases, known rank, iid Gaussian noise, and uniform nuclear-norm honesty: the scan found entrywise, functional, Frobenius, and asymptotic results, but no matched polynomial-time upper and all-procedure lower frontier.
